what_its_for: Tavaborole is a prescription antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the toenails (onychomycosis). It works by killing the fungus that causes the nail infection.
how_to_take: Apply one drop of tavaborole solution directly to the affected toenail(s) once daily at bedtime. Use the dropper provided to apply the medicine. Spread it over the entire nail surface and under the tip of the nail as much as possible. Let the medicine dry completely before putting on socks or footwear. Wash your hands after applying. Do not swallow this medicine — it is for use on the nails only.
dosing: Apply once daily to each affected toenail at bedtime. Treatment lasts for 48 weeks (about 11 months). Do not use more than directed or stop early without talking to your doctor.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular routine. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Keep away from heat and open flame, as the solution is flammable.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting tavaborole in your eyes, mouth, nose, or vagina. Do not use nail polish or other nail cosmetics on the treated nails unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid exposing the solution to open flames, as it is flammable. Keep the treated nails clean and dry as much as possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice: redness, swelling, or increased irritation around the treated nail; blistering, burning, or peeling of the skin around the nail; signs of a new or worsening infection; no improvement after several months of use; any allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat.
when_it_works: Fungal nail infections are very slow to clear up. Most people do not see results for several months. The full course of treatment is 48 weeks. Even if your nail looks better, continue using the medicine for the full time prescribed. Nails grow slowly, so it may take additional months after treatment ends to see a completely clear, healthy nail.
special_populations: Tavaborole has not been studied in children under 6 years old, so it is not recommended for very young children. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine. If you are breastfeeding, avoid applying tavaborole to areas that may come into contact with your baby. Older adults can generally use this medicine safely, but always follow your doctor's guidance.
